name: Uranium
occurrence: Found combined in uraninite (pitchblende) ore; the heaviest naturally occurring element found in significant quantities on Earth.
majorUses: Depleted uranium armour and armour-piercing ammunition (very high density)
safetyNotes: Both radiotoxic and chemically toxic as a heavy metal; enrichment and handling are tightly regulated worldwide under international nuclear non-proliferation frameworks.
notableCharacteristics: Its fission — splitting a uranium-235 nucleus with a neutron to release enormous energy plus more neutrons — is the physical process behind both nuclear power plants and the first atomic bombs.
ncertRelevance: discovery and Klaproth's naming after the planet Uranus
whyHere: Uranium-235's nucleus is just unstable enough to split apart when struck by a neutron, releasing more neutrons and energy in a self-sustaining chain reaction — the exact physical mechanism that makes uranium usable as both a nuclear fuel and a weapon.
didYouKnow: Klaproth named uranium after the planet Uranus, which had been discovered only eight years earlier in 1781 — making uranium the first element named after a planet.
genZNote: Named after a planet discovered eight years earlier, then went on to literally split the atom. Overachiever, immediately.
